# Author-source validation report

Scope: 161 datasets and 175 registered contrasts; `macaque_snrna` is explicitly excluded. Each ledger row carries its own review date. Completion of recorded audit checks does not imply full scientific verification.

## Scientific verification

These are detailed author-reproduction classifications, retained separately from the primary internal-QC and author-concordance badges. See `../quality/QUALITY_REPORT.generated.md` and `../quality/assessments.generated.json` for the current processing-quality decisions and individual checklists.

| Evidence claim | Datasets |
|---|---:|
| Fully verified | 0 |
| Author results compared, limits remain | 72 |
| Author effects reconstructed | 5 |
| Author results untested | 32 |
| No comparison evidence | 0 |
| Unresolved, review required | 52 |
| Verification in progress | 0 |
| Outside verification scope | 1 |

| Author-result availability | Datasets |
|---|---:|
| Author results accessible; see comparison scope | 57 |
| Author result file located; retrieval not confirmed | 0 |
| Only partial or non-equivalent author results available | 95 |
| Comparable author results not located in reviewed sources | 7 |
| Author-result access blocked or restricted | 2 |
| Author-result availability not yet reviewed | 0 |
| Not assessed: outside scope | 1 |

Full verification requires explicit contrast-level sign-off, byte/content source evidence, exact output trace, and comparable author results with no unresolved cohort, effect, statistical, or coverage limitations. A high correlation, a selected gene, a source checksum, or a completed checklist is insufficient. Unreviewed availability is not recorded as unavailable data. Unavailable data is not recorded as a mismatch. See the application Data verification workflow page and the per-dataset reasons/next steps in the TSV.

Comparability is documented separately for samples/replication, biological contrast, gene identifiers and tested universe, effect definition, statistical inference, and reference coverage. These are mandatory scientific requirements, not weighted points. Every record identifies the result being checked, author reference, criteria, limitations and conclusion. A separate author-method reconstruction does not verify the registered Explorer output by inheritance. Missing author P/FDR values are unassessed, not nonsignificant; selected tables and empty significant sets do not establish full-universe agreement.

The status levels are intentionally not interchangeable. `Processed source match` means the local processed input matches the author-deposited source. `Author result match` requires a direct comparison with an author result table. `Pipeline output trace` independently verifies that each published bundle row came from the committed local analysis table.

Downloaded manuscripts, supplementary workbooks, and author notebooks used in continued manual review are byte-pinned in `continued-sources/README.md`.

## Pathway rebuild and provenance checks

Cache-isolated FGSEA outputs were rebuilt and schema-3 provenance/checksums verified for 160 datasets and 174 registered contrasts. The changes below compare with pre-audit local outputs; they are not author-result comparisons and do not change the validation statuses above.

143 datasets use Git baseline commit `25cb4827a7385181e3fd09713be39ebda80ca13c`. 17 dataset(s) use a hash-pinned pre-migration local snapshot because no committed baseline exists.

- [GSE281503](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE281503): Pre-migration local snapshot: the original processed files dated 2026-08-31 are in a Git-ignored dataset directory and have no committed baseline. These copies were captured before the cache-isolated FGSEA rebuild; they are local pipeline outputs, not author-generated pathway results.

| [GSE284408](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE284408) | Review required | Figure 3E establishes the two counts. The Results text reports 389, and Table S1 contains 299 unique IDs. The reason for including rows 129–138 and the exact gene lists supplied to the enrichment analyses remain undocumented. The comparison covers the same six libraries. Animal identities, pooling and independence across libraries remain undocumented in the examined sources. The registered fit sums source counts for 32 published symbols, including Kiss1. Individual source-feature tests cannot be assigned to those aggregate symbols. FDR calls depend on the model and tested family. The deposited table matches the input SHA-256 in registered provenance. GEO, ENA, the sample sheet and the model identify the same three NCD and three HFD male ARC libraries. The deposited effects are log2 ratios of group-mean FPKM, with zero means exported as 0.001. The registered edgeR-QL effects are coefficients fitted to TMM-normalized counts. Across 14,119 one-to-one pairs, Pearson is 0.92695 and Spearman is 0.92135. Signs agree for 12,891 of 14,093 pairs with two nonzero effects. All seven registered FDR < 0.05 calls occur among the 19 author calls. The historical DESeq2 refit is a separate sensitivity analysis. Figure 3E labels 164 up and 125 down. All 289 GEO features meeting nominal P < 0.05 and an unsigned fold change > 1.5 occur in Table S1. Its ten additional rows pass nominal P but fall below the fold cutoff in both the workbook and GEO. All 230 distinct symbols listed in Table S2 occur among the qualifying Table S1 labels. Using Table S1 pathway annotations, the qualifying set reproduces the up and down counts in all 229 Table S3 KEGG pathways. Including all 299 rows changes 19 of those counts by pathway and adds two pathway IDs. The article reports no original code. |
| [GSE167264](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE167264) | Review required | Npy’s adjusted Figure 5b ranks and the registered coefficient have opposite directions. The GEO counts and registered effective library sizes reproduce Npy means of 34.447 TMM CPM in ob/ob and 19.159 in WT. The plotting code removes batch and tissue effects. Each of the 24 batch labels belongs to a single genotype/diet group, and the batch adjustment specifies no design to preserve group differences. Which step accounts for the reversal remains unresolved. The paper’s Lepr narrative conflicts with the normal-diet sample colors. Ghsr’s rank crossing leaves the direction of its displayed group-mean difference indeterminate. Four figure-selected genes have no published normal-diet coefficient magnitudes, P values or FDR. The Figshare interaction answers a different question. The legacy source has no committed source-file checksum manifest. This review pins the fresh public downloads and verifies the registered table against its recorded output SHA-256. The registered DE table and local per-gene track both yield 52 genes with BH FDR < 0.05. The local qc_global.js summary records nSig = 910 for the same track. The GEO family SOFT links Ahmed et al.’s published article. Its author-hosted journal PDF gives genotype, diet and expression color for all twelve hypothalamic libraries in Figure 5b. The six normal-diet library labels agree across GEO, the count header and the registered sample sheet. Each BioSample maps to one ENA run. Among the three ordered values per genotype, Lepr and Agrp are higher in ob/ob at every rank and Npy is lower. Ghsr has a higher ob/ob median and crossing ranks. The registered edgeR-QL coefficients are positive for all four genes. The paper describes suppression of Lepr in ob/ob. The Figshare Hy worksheet exports the DESeq2 interaction. Source files, mappings and the independent replay are in data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE167264/codex-2026-11-21/. |
| [GSE292416](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE292416) | Review required | The 16 GEO records describe hypothalamic tissue. The eight registered IP libraries match by title and genotype. The source identifies four-mouse pools by replicate label. Individual mouse identifiers and an ARC-only dissection are undocumented. Of 89 registered FDR calls, four have a linked author row with missing genotype FDR and one is a multi-ID aggregate. The deposited author table provides adjusted P values only. The previous manual review describes an earlier registered table. The current built-in symbol comparison pairs 13,116 genes, including five conflicting source-ID matches and 31 registered aggregates. The source-ID comparison uses the deposited count matrix and the registered feature map. Index excerpts of the publisher’s Results, Figure 4B, STAR Methods and code-availability statement support the reported thresholds and counts. Direct requests for the publisher article and PDF returned HTTP 403. The paper-access designation falls back to the existing source inventory when this manual record replaces the previous one. The paper’s 236 is reproduced as a count. Figure 4B reports 3,550 enriched genes, while the deposit supports 2,348 distinct enriched IDs. The historical DESeq2 fit and figure membership remain open. The separate raw-count reconstruction provides no registered-output sign-off. WT and KO each contribute four hypothalamic PNOC-IP pools to the genotype comparison. The 13,946 one-to-one Ensembl pairs have Pearson 0.999799 and Spearman 0.999776. Of 13,946 nonzero pairs, 13,545 agree in sign. At FDR < 0.05, DESeq2 calls 1,049 paired genes and edgeR-QL calls 84. All 84 are shared. Applying the paper and GEO rules to the full deposit gives 236 and 69 joint calls. Under the paper rule, 2,048 WT and 1,502 KO enrichment calls include 1,202 IDs in both groups. The union contains 2,348 IDs, of which 2,197 have finite genotype results for both volcano axes. The paper reports 3,550 enriched genes. Summing the arm counts gives that number, but the authors’ plotting IDs and counting procedure remain unknown. The selection.tsv file records rule-derived joint calls. |

| [GSE328990](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE328990) | Review required | Both numerical concordance routes fall below the project thresholds despite 99.48% registered coverage. The RNA came from whole hypothalamus of 16-week-old gonadal-intact females, with two animals per pool. GEO calls the controls wildtype and the registry uses WT. The manuscript’s Animals section identifies the controls as homozygous C451A floxed littermates. The count matrix matches the registered input SHA-256, and the deposited DESeq2 table matches the original-source SHA-256 in the comparison spec. Of 18,480 registered symbols, 18,383 have one-to-one effects. Pearson is 0.8955, Spearman is 0.8630, and 16,085 of 18,383 nonzero pairs agree in direction. Among 18,377 pairs with finite FDR, the authors have 28 discoveries and the registered analysis has four, all shared. All 18 effect and raw-P pairs in Supplementary Table 4 identify unique deposited rows at printed precision. Gm49510 has a small printed FDR discrepancy. All 15 individually comparable paper hits agree in direction. Fam205a3 (Spata31f1d in the pre-fit map) and Gm8116 fall below the required number of expressing pools. The registered Nlrp5-ps coefficient combines two input features. Cenpf is lower in the mutant pools in both analyses, with deposited log2FC −2.2713 and registered log2FC −0.1348. The public files do not identify the cause. See continued-sources/GSE328990/codex-2026-11-21/refute/verify.py for the independent replay. |

| [GSE185074](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE185074) | Review required | Seven GEO sample titles and count columns identify the registered control IP libraries. The GSM genotype field says IRmKate2, while the TRAP methods describe Cre-treated IRwt/wt reporter controls. The exact construct assignment for those pools needs clarification. The publisher’s interaction column equals both differences of simple effects. That identity leaves the dispersion-estimation cohort, pool terms, Salmon import, length offsets and filter order undetermined. Registered-output coverage is below 90%. Several input features can share a published symbol. The two exports omit raw diet P values, and eight author diet adjusted P values are missing. The GEO marker flag and the red Figure 8b category describe different selections. Both marker comparisons are secondary to the full-table comparison. The registered contrast uses four HFD and three NCD IP pools. GEO and the Figure 8b source sheet report the same author analysis to workbook precision. The IDF identifies day 8 as the collection time and leaves the publication title, DOI and PubMed ID blank. All 32 measurement columns in raw_counts.tsv match SDRF libraries. Eight are hypothalamus libraries from four DSS mice and four controls. ENA lists the reads. NCBI returned zero GEO links for the BioProject and the eight BioSamples, and the searches located no matching GSE, GSM or sample supplement. D’Alessio et al. report hypothalamic RNA-seq under PRJNA1378229. Its six DSS libraries are labeled day 6, and none of its 12 BioSample accessions occurs in E-MTAB-15489. |
| [GSE337822](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE337822) | Source unavailable | Author effect sizes, P values and FDR remain unassessed in excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons and non-neuronal cells. GSE337822 contains 20 mice, with five females and five males per treatment arm. Its 180 sample files comprise 60 feature-by-nucleus count matrices with matching feature and barcode lists. The series matrix contains zero gene rows. The registered edgeR models compare isoflurane with oxygen within each broad population and adjust for sex. GEO describes responses within cell clusters. The accession, publication and repository searches through 2026-11-22 UTC located no author gene-level effects for the registered populations. GSE243489 supplied the cell taxonomy and compares recovery sleep with undisturbed sleep in a separate cohort. |
| [GSE262407](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE262407) | Review required | Figure 2g pairs 5,350 of 9,857 registered genes. Coverage of the registered output is below the 90% requirement for a full author table. The ARC/VMH column in Supplementary Figure 5a contains the genes shared between regions. Its coefficients and five shared-gene FDR calls differ from SD1. The Ghrh, OPC and oligodendrocyte comparisons are sensitive to low-nucleus mouse exclusions. The authors' whole-population DE donor lists are unavailable in the pinned code. Sixteen population–contrast pairs have no matching author coefficient in the reviewed sources. Nominal-P lists, genes shared between regions and effects-only panels support only their stated scopes. Including Arc15 gives 5,350 of 5,350 Figure 2g genes, with a maximum absolute log2FC difference of 1.07674e-10. Applying the Figure 2c PCA mouse cutoff to the DE fit loses 10 published genes and adds six. With Arc15, the fit also reproduces all 529 selected control-diet astrocyte glucose effects in Supplementary Data 1 (SD1) to within 4.172e-10. The 510 genes shared with Supplementary Figure 5a agree in sign. Their median absolute log2FC difference is 0.004650 and the maximum is 0.078297. At FDR < 0.05, 70 shared genes are called in both sources, two only in SD1 and three only in the figure. SD3 and GEO count 75,862 nuclei, including 5,588 ARC/VMH astrocytes. The paper reports 75,787. Its regional totals localize the 75-nucleus difference to DVC neurons. See comparisons.json, refit-metrics.tsv and refute/ in data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE262407/codex-2026-11-21. |
| [GSE113576](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE113576) | Review required | GEO and the linked ENA records describe three mice per sequencing pool. GEO lists postnatal days 60–70 for all six libraries. The sequencing methods on supplement p. 2 describe tissue from four to five mice per sex per replicate at approximately seven to eight weeks of age. The registry's stated total of 18 mice comes from GEO. The sources establish six library replicates, while donor counts and ages for the individual pools remain unresolved. Author effect concordance and inference for male_vs_female remain unassessed. All nine attachments listed by PMC and BioStudies were recovered, covering Figures S1–S22 and Tables S1–S11. All 31,299 Table S1 barcodes, sex labels and replicate numbers match GEO. The registered analysis sums cells within each of six pools, including 841 cells labeled ambiguous and 88 labeled unstable in Table S1's major cell class. The authors excluded these classes from subsequent cluster analyses. Table S2 summarizes neuronal clusters across sexes. Figure S8 shows selected sections from two male and two female animals for 11 genes with previously reported sex differences. Dryad provides per-cell spatial measurements. The reviewed material supplies no effect, raw P or FDR for the registered contrast. |
| [GSE224274](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE224274) | Review required | Six pairs of differently spelled labels share current MGI marker IDs. In Ensembl release 102 for GRCm38, Ccdc121 and 4930548H24Rik are on different chromosomes, and 4933403O08Rik and Tex16 have separate gene IDs. The authors’ annotation and stable feature IDs are needed to evaluate these candidates. Four Figure 1c labels survive only as dates in that sheet. With zero source-confirmed effect pairs, effect direction, magnitude, raw-P and FDR agreement remain unassessed. The 12 registered library labels match the GEO sample records. All 69,168 CPM values in the deposited matrix equal the registered inputs for those genes and libraries. Figure 1c reports six mice per arm and SENS relative to NEO. Its workbook gives group-level log2 fold changes and −log10 P values without individual library IDs or adjusted P values. The registered limma coefficient is mean log2(CPM + 1) in SENS minus the mean in NEO. The registered DE table retains 5,143 of 5,764 deposited rows after variance filtering. All 621 excluded rows are zero throughout. None of the 14,952 readable figure labels matches either table by spelling, including after case folding. GEO mentions a 10-read cutoff. The available files do not identify the featureCounts rows selected for the figure and the deposit. |
| [GSE308884](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE308884) | Review required | Figure S6C reports 14 diet-up/drug-down and 12 diet-down/drug-up intersections before one exclusion. The 25 printed Figure 4E genes give 11 and 14 in the registered tables. The published diagram gives counts without gene identities. The authors used a protein-coding, TMM-normalized, sample-weighted voomLmFit analysis. HypoExplorer fitted unweighted limma to deposited log2 CPM. The contribution of each difference to the diet discovery discrepancy is unknown. The ten volcano labels belong to the 25-gene heatmap set. The evidence falls below the 30-paired-gene minimum for author-concordance-v2 in each contrast. In Figures 4C and S6B, the same 10 genes match the registered signs in both contrasts. The authors class all 10 as discoveries in DIO vehicle versus lean and report zero treatment discoveries at 10% FDR. Zero of the 10 registered rows reach 10% FDR in either contrast. All 25 Figure 4E genes reverse in the registered results, but their directional counts differ from the authors’ selection diagram. |
